label: build:core
mission: Renderer setup, fixed-step physics loop, state machine (menu, intro, countdown, racing, finished, pause), lap/checkpoint/position logic, chase/hood/bumper cameras, keyboard and gamepad input, barrier and car-car collisions, effect/audio/HUD wiring, window.__game debug API and URL params for automated tests.

structured_report.summary:
I built the full game core for MIDNIGHT APEX, and the game now plays end to end with the real modules from the other agents. Verified flows: menu, intro, countdown, racing, pause, finish cinematic, results, restart. A full 3-lap autopilot race at timescale 3 finished with all 5 cars, showed results, restarted cleanly and logged no errors. The browser console is clean on the main page.

**Bootstrap (main.js, index.html, style.css)**
- WebGL check, then a dark pulsing loading veil with status text. It fades out on the first rendered frame, so there is no white flash.
- Renderer settings: high-performance, antialias off, sRGB, ACES tone mapping at exposure 1.0, shadows on. Pixel ratio is min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5) on high and 1 on low.
- Adaptive resolution: if frames average over 19 ms for 2 s, the pixel ratio steps down by 0.125 (never below 1.0 on high, 0.75 on low). `?drs=0` turns it off.
- Shaders are precompiled behind the veil (`compileAsync` with a 6 s cap), then one warm-up render runs.
- Resize is handled and the canvas context menu is blocked.

**Loop and state machine (game.js)**
- `setAnimationLoop` with dt clamped to 0.1 s and the URL/API timescale applied.
- Fixed physics step of `CONFIG.physics.fixedDt` with an accumulator. Max sub-steps scale with timescale; extra time is dropped rather than spiralling.
- AI runs every 2nd step (60 Hz of game time). Collisions run on every sub-step. Car transforms are interpolated for rendering.
- Every subsystem call is wrapped so a failing module logs once and the loop keeps going. The whole frame is also wrapped, because three's animation loop stops if its callback throws.
- States:
  - **menu**: four-shot attract camera on the grid.
  - **intro**: 2.6 s sweep from the front of the car to the chase position, with a track/laps banner. Restart uses a 1.8 s intro.
  - **countdown**: 3-2-1-GO with beeps. Cars are held; the core simulates free-revving and AI throttle blips. At GO, revs in the window give a "PERFECT LAUNCH" or "GOOD LAUNCH" boost; bouncing off the limiter gives none.
  - **racing**.
  - **finished**: the player switches to autopilot and the camera eases into an orbit. Results appear when everyone finishes (after at least 6 s) or after 25 s. DNF times are estimated from progress.
  - **paused**: Esc/P, and automatically when the tab is hidden.
- Enter restarts cleanly: grid reset, particles cleared, AI state reset, timers and HUD reset.

**Race logic (race.js)**
- Progress = laps × length + distance past the start line, kept continuous across the line in both directions.
- A lap only counts on a forward crossing with all three sector checkpoints passed. A Node unit test confirmed that reversing over the line or skipping checkpoints does not score.
- Lap, total, best and last times; positions use finish order first, then progress, sorted without allocation.
- Wrong-way warning after 1 s at more than 110° from the track direction, repeated every 1.6 s.
- On-screen messages: LAP x/y, FINAL LAP, NEW BEST LAP, FINISHED/YOU WIN.
- Drift chain (drift > 0.4 for more than 1 s), with a multiplier, handed to the HUD's drift meter.

**Collisions (collisions.js)**
- Barrier: all four corners are checked against the wall offset, with a curvature correction.
  - The car is pushed back inside; bounce drops from 0.3 to 0.08 as impact speed rises; friction scales with the hit; scraping adds drag.
  - Glancing hits turn the car parallel to the wall and cancel the spin the impulse would add, so the car deflects and scrapes instead of spinning across the road.
  - Measured: a 24° hit at 252 km/h leaves the car at 205 km/h, aligned with the wall.
- Car vs car: each car is three circles along its length. Overlap is split by mass, and the impulse (with yaw lever and friction) goes through `applyImpulse`.
  - Measured rear-end at 140 km/h closing speed: momentum conserved, restitution about 0.21, closest approach 4.56 m (bumper to bumper), no tunnelling.
- Effects on impact: sparks, impact and scrape sounds, post-fx flash and camera shake.

**Camera (camera.js)**
- Chase-far / chase-near: base distance and height as specified (6.2 m / 2.0 m for chase-far), look-ahead, yaw lag that blends toward the velocity direction so drifts swing the car out, braking/acceleration lag, a slight bank into corners.
  - FOV goes 62°→85° with speed plus a 6° nitro kick, with a partial dolly-zoom so the car keeps its on-screen size at high speed.
  - High-speed buzz above about 235 km/h and impact shake; never below 0.3 m; kept out of buildings near barriers.
- Hood and bumper cams are fitted to the actual car model by ray-casting its body.
- Scripted shots: menu attract (four shots), intro sweep, finish orbit with a car-relative blend.

**Input (input.js)**
- Keyboard uses `e.code`, with steering ramps of about 6/s up and 10/s down, mild lock reduction at speed (physics adds its own), and pedal ramps.
- Gamepad: RT/LT, left stick with deadzone, A/X handbrake, B/RB nitro, Y camera, Start pause, Back reset, A confirm.
- Arrow keys and Space don't scroll the page; held keys clear when the window loses focus; the first key or click unlocks audio.

**Effects and audio (effects.js, audiomix.js)**
- Called once per frame per source, as the particle module expects.
- Particles: wet spray behind the tyres plus a mist wake, smoke and skid marks per wheel, nitro and backfire flames at the exhausts.
- Car model state each frame: brake/reverse lights, steering, wheel spin, pitch/roll, nitro glow.
- Audio:
  - Engine and wind.
  - The four nearest opponents with pan and distance.
  - Skid, nitro, gear shifts and backfire pops.
  - Impacts and scrapes, quieter with distance for AI cars.
  - Rain catches the player's headlight beams.

**Bench and test tools (dev/core.html)**
- `dev/core.html` runs the full game with Vite's hot-reload socket stubbed out, so long playtests aren't interrupted by reloads from other agents' saves.
- `__game.runScript()` runs input scripts on game time and captures canvas screenshots. That kept the drift, ram, wall, nitro and launch tests reliable while the machine was under very heavy load.
structured_report.contract_notes:
**Deviations**
- three r186 removed `PCFSoftShadowMap`, so I used `PCFShadowMap`, which now does soft filtering.
- The intro is 2.6 s.
- The player starts in slot floor(total × 0.6), which is slot 3 of 5 (4th on the grid).
- R reset places the car on the centerline, but drops into the adjacent ±4.5 m lane if a rival is there. It gives 2 s with no car-car collisions and a blink.

**Optional extras I use from other modules (each guarded, harmless if absent)**
- **Track:** `track.project(pos, hintS, out)` with an out object to avoid allocations; the world implementation supports it.
- **HUD:**
  - `state.drift` is the object form `{active, score, multiplier}`; the HUD pops the banked score when `active` drops.
  - `gear` 0 shows as N before the race.
  - Extra state fields: `driftTotal`, `wrongWay`, `mode`, `throttle`, `brake`, `steer`, and `name`/`position` on each car entry.
  - `showMenu` also gets `laps` and `racers`.
  - `hud.setSoundHandler` is wired to `audio.playUI`.
  - Results colours are '#rrggbb' strings.
- **Audio:**
  - `setPaused` on pause/resume.
  - `setMuted(true)` for `?mute=1`.
  - I don't call `setMasterVolume` on tab hide because the audio module suspends its own context.
  - Music and ambience are switched on when audio initialises.
- **Rain:** `setHeadlights(pos, dir, on)` every frame. The beam origin is pushed forward in the hood and bumper views, and switched off when the camera is in front of the lamps.
- **Car model:**
  - `model.body` is used for the hood/bumper camera ray-cast.
  - `model.spotLights` are dimmed to 1.5% while a low camera sits inside the beam. This fixes a severe white-out from wet-road specular in the menu hero shot and intro sweep.
  - The headlight decal (found as the root's additive mesh) is hidden while the camera is above its footprint. This also covers a rival right behind the chase camera.
- **Physics:**
  - `controls.hold` while cars are held on the grid.
  - `backfireCount` triggers backfire sounds and flames.
  - `inertia` is used in collision maths.
  - `syncGear()` is used by the teleport test API.
- **Particles:**
  - The car's unscaled velocity goes to spray and smoke; the module derives the fling motion itself.
  - `emitSparks` gets the 4th velocity argument.
  - `clear()` runs on restart.
- **Postfx:** `setSize` is called with CSS pixels; the composer pixel ratio follows the renderer.

**Extra debug API (contract API unchanged)**
- On `window.__game`: `restart`, `pause`, `resume`, `showResults`, `setCamera(mode)`, `teleport(s, lateral, speed)`, `runScript(steps)` (game-time input scripts with canvas captures), `scriptDone`, `scriptShots`, and getters for `game`, `renderer`, `scene`, `camera`.
- `getTelemetry()` also returns `lapsDone`, `progress`, `raceTime`, `bestLap`, `nitro`, `drift`, `camera`, `autopilot`, `drawCalls`, `triangles`, `pixelRatio`, `cpuMs` (per-section CPU time) and `errors` (subsystem failure counts).

**Extra controls**
- `?drs=0` turns off adaptive resolution.
- The ` (backquote) key toggles the debug overlay, which now also shows per-section CPU time.

**New file I created:** `dev/core.html`, the hot-reload-proof bench.
known_issues: The player's SpotLights reflecting off the near-mirror wet road blow out the whole frame when a low camera looks into the headlights. Core dims the lights in-beam as a workaround, but the car or world owner may want to lower the intensity or raise the road roughness for that case.

Car models are heavy: about 32 draw calls and about 200k triangles per car per frame, counting shadow and reflection passes. Race views total 140–330 draw calls and 1.0–2.2M triangles. LOD or skipping distant AI in the reflection pass would help.

Early in the session, full-black frames appeared after GO with post-processing on (suspected bad pixels spreading through bloom). They disappeared after I switched to calling each particle emitter once per frame and the fx module was updated, and a 16-frame check with all AI using nitro was clean. If they come back, suspect a bad value entering bloom from a particle shader.

The keyboard perfect launch is a timing skill: from idle, a held throttle passes through the rev window about 0.23–0.48 s after pressing, so you press just before GO. The HUD shows no launch window or indicator.
AI laps are about 75–80 s (first lap about 80 s from a standing start), at the top of the contract's 55–75 s target. The AI keeps a fairly fixed running order. Both belong to dynamics.
Gamepad mapping was code-reviewed only; no hardware was available. Auto-pause on tab hide was not testable headless (the logic is simple).

The machine was extremely loaded during testing (load average 60–90), so the FPS from the harness is not meaningful. Performance was judged from draw calls, triangles and measured CPU time per section instead.
The hood view also shows the player's headlight pool lit by the real spot lights. The additive decal is hidden there, so it looks natural, but it is bright.
structured_report.perf_notes:
**Core CPU per frame (measured)**
- Simulation for 5 cars (physics at 120 Hz, AI at 60 Hz, barrier and car-car collisions on every sub-step) and race logic: 0.1–0.4 ms.
- Camera, effects emission, particles and rain update: 0.05–0.2 ms.
- HUD and audio wiring: 0.2–0.4 ms.

**Other modules, measured through core's timers**
- World update, including submitting the planar reflection pass: 0.5–2.4 ms.
- Render and post-fx submission: 0.6–2.8 ms.

**Allocations**
- No per-frame allocations in core hot paths:
  - vectors and objects are reused, and `project` gets an out object;
  - wrapped subsystem calls use pre-bound functions;
  - the HUD state and audio opponent list are reused;
  - positions are sorted with an allocation-free insertion sort.

**GPU load**
- 140–330 draw calls and 1.0–2.2M triangles depending on the view, mostly from the car models and the environment.

**Resolution and loading**
- Pixel ratio is min(DPR, 1.5) on high and 1 on low.
- Adaptive resolution steps down if the 2 s average frame time exceeds 19 ms (floor 1.0 high, 0.75 low).
- Shaders are precompiled behind the veil and followed by a warm-up render, so the first lap doesn't hitch.

**Particle budget**
- AI cars beyond 170 m emit nothing.
- Within range, AI cars spray only from the rear wheels; skid marks stop beyond 120 m and smoke beyond 60 m.
